newsitem.title: UK: Mediterranean oil products flat but LS fuel climbs.
newsitem.headline: Mediterranean oil products flat but LS fuel climbs.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly steady, but low sulphur fuel rose in late trading.

Gasoline steadied in late business after taking an early dip with crude and products futures. Traders said the market was beginning to look better balanced with maintenance and poor reforming margins eating into refinery output.
They said recent sales into the Lebanon had also helped draw down lengthy low octane supplies.
Naphtha held steady with only only one prompt cargo offered. The 60kt October 3-4 loading Skikda cargo was offered into the Med and NWE at around benchmark quotes high +$3-$3.50 a tonne.
The seller, Petrobras, said they had some interest, but said the cargo also had transatlantic arbitrage options if it failed to achieve a satisfactory bid in Europe.
High gas oil prices kept most buyers to the sidelines except those with urgent requirements.

Russian material was valued at quotes cif high +$1/$2 basis Genoa, but those holding cargoes were reluctant to show offers for fear of pushing prices lower. "There's no buying for early October Russian," said one Geneva-based trader.
Demand for low sulphur diesel was seen covered through most of October.
Retailers in Greece and Portugal continued to sell 0.2 percent sulphur despite today's introduction of new EU emission rules, traders said.
High sulphur fuel was flat amid expectation among many traders that prices were likely to firm over the next few days.
High sulphur cargoes remain well bid around $2.50 a tonne above the quotations for good quality Italian refinery barrels but nearer $5.50 for Tunisian grades.
Low sulphur rose about $2 after swaps talked up to $124.50 for Oct late. Despite poor Enel demand, trade demand and some demand into Israel propped the market --London +44 171 542 7456
